title: Introduction to Machine Learning
content: Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence that enables computers to learn patterns from data and make predictions or decisions.

title: Supervised Learning
content: Supervised learning uses labeled data to learn the relationship between input features and target values. Regression predicts continuous values, while classification predicts categories.

title: Unsupervised Learning
content: Unsupervised learning works with data without labeled target values. It is commonly used to discover hidden patterns, groups, and structures in datasets.

title: Overfitting
content: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too closely and performs poorly on unseen data. Cross-validation and regularization can help reduce overfitting.

title: What is RAG
content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines information retrieval with a language model. Relevant information is retrieved from an external knowledge source and provided as context to the model.

title: Document Loading
content: A document loader converts files such as PDFs, text files, web pages, and other sources into documents that can be processed by a RAG pipeline.

title: Text Chunking
content: Large documents are divided into smaller chunks before creating embeddings. Chunk size and overlap can affect retrieval quality.

title: Embeddings
content: Embeddings are numerical representations of text that capture semantic information. Similar pieces of text tend to have similar vector representations.

title: Vector Search
content: A vector database stores embeddings and can retrieve documents that are semantically similar to a user's query.

title: RAG Retrieval
content: During retrieval, the user's query is converted into an embedding and relevant document chunks are selected from the vector store.
